title: A case of long QT syndrome: challenges on a bumpy road
case_prompt:
A 28-year-old pregnant woman with a history of epilepsy treated with phenytoin was referred to cardiology for premature ventricular complexes (PVCs). She had two prior miscarriages at gestational weeks 8 and 21 due to suspected cervical insufficiency; during the current pregnancy a cerclage was placed and intravenous terbutaline was given to forestall preterm labor. She reported new-onset palpitations. 

On initial ECG during sinus rhythm at 90 beats/min, there were frequent monomorphic PVCs, second-degree atrioventricular (AV) 2:1 block, and a manually measured QT interval of 520 msec in lead V₅. The PVCs had a left bundle-branch–block configuration in lead V₁, suggesting a right ventricular origin. A 24-hour ambulatory ECG off terbutaline showed PVCs 10% of the time, three brief runs of nonsustained ventricular tachycardia, and five episodes of bigeminal PVCs. Transthoracic echocardiography, including right ventricular views, excluded structural heart disease.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Structural heart disease was excluded — “Echocardiography, including right ventricular projections, excluded structural heart disease.”  
2. Acquired QT prolongation from electrolyte imbalance or QT-prolonging drugs was considered and ruled out — “It is important to rule out alternative explanations for QT prolongation. Such causes might include acquired myocardial conduction delays or low levels of potassium, magnesium, or calcium, as well as taking QT‐prolonging drugs.”  
3. Terbutaline-induced QT prolongation was considered but did not fully account for persistent findings — “Adrenergic response is known prolong the QT interval, and in this case terbutaline unmasked the LQTS and led to diagnosis.”  
4. Epilepsy as a cause of transient loss of consciousness was reconsidered and deemed unlikely — “However, our patient had a negative electroencephalogram, a history more typical for a cardiac disorder, and genetic mutations pathognomonic for LQTS.”  
5. The second-degree AV block was interpreted as functional from prolonged repolarization rather than intrinsic conduction disease — “This may be interpreted as functional AV block due to prolonged ventricular repolarization.”  
6. Congenital long QT syndrome was suspected based on marked QT prolongation and ventricular arrhythmias — “Long QT syndrome (LQTS) was suspected.”
